findings.title: Monitor context returns original config instead of the modified copy
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies `monitor_environment.monitor.config` into `config` and, when `schedule_type` is present, replaces it with the display value. However the returned dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` on line 168, not the modified `config`. The copy and display conversion are dead code, so `schedule_type` is emitted as the raw stored value (for example an int/enum) instead of the intended display string in the occurrence context.

findings.title: Incident can be triggered before reaching failure_issue_threshold
findings.body: For `failure_issue_threshold > 1`, the code slices the latest `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins but does not verify that there actually are that many. On a new or sparse monitor, after the first failed check-in `previous_checkins` contains only that one failure; the `any(... == CheckInStatus.OK)` check is false, so the monitor is set to ERROR and an incident is created even though the configured consecutive-failure threshold has not been met. This defeats the user-configured threshold and can cause premature monitor alerts.
